core.title: Journey runner composes flow routers without executing user/system flows or product capabilities
core.given: A repository with a composition root declares one or more journey topology plan artifacts (whether or not the user/system flows runtime layer or a journey runner exists yet)
core.when: the journey topology is present, which enables the obligation on the user/system flows runtime layer
core.then: You MUST ship a journey runner in the user/system flows runtime layer that acts only as continuation control: it reads and parses the declared journey topology and delegates every routing decision to the flow router runner using declaration-derived values, never executing user/system flows, product capabilities or flow variables itself.
prefer: If no journey runner exists, add one in the user/system flows runtime layer that reads the supplied journey declaration; its absence is a violation, not an option.

The intended call model is: composition root -> journey runner -> flow router runner (routing entry methods) -> user/system flow runner executes the selected user/system flow -> inspect declared continuation/terminal -> next flow router runner ... (the user/system flow runner's execution step is invoked by the flow router runner, never by the journey runner).

The flow router runner selects exactly one user/system flow and delegates it to the user/system flow runner; the journey runner only decides which flow router is entered next per the declared topology.
avoid: Constructing a flow router runner from a hardcoded literal path.
Referencing the user/system flow runner, importing product capability modules, or invoking the user/system-flow-execution entry point from the journey runner.
Looping over the declared user/system flow sequence as an executor in the journey runner.
Carrying or mutating flow variables in the journey runner.
Putting cross-interlocking topology into the flow router runner.
unless: No journey topology plan artifacts: no journey runner obligation.
No composition root yet (planning stage): no journey runner obligation, as the sibling interlocking-runner existence rule owes no flow router runner before one.
core.why: Each layer owns only its responsibility (journey runner: continuation control, never the user/system flow step loop; flow router runner: local route selection; user/system flow runner: sole wagon-step executor), so topology cannot bypass routing or duplicate user/system flow execution.
evidence: A journey runner exists in the user/system flows runtime layer whenever the activation prerequisites hold.
Journey runner source shows reading and parsing of a journey declaration and references the flow router runner.

No literal-path interlocking-runner construction, user/system-flow-runner reference, product capability import, user/system-flow-execution entry-point call, declared-user/system-flow-sequence executor loop or flow-variable handling in the journey runner.
verification: The check enforces the runtime boundary introduced by planner journey topology: presence of the journey topology plan artifacts (located by the profile's plan-artifact path pattern) enables the obligation; there is no phase or edit-event gate. The check must run, and report a missing runner, even when the user/system flows runtime layer is absent.

A structural check looks for the journey runner (the stack's runner construct named by the profile) in the user/system flows runtime layer; it requires evidence that the runtime reads and parses a journey declaration, requires a reference to the flow router runner, rejects literal interlocking-runner construction, and rejects direct user-system-flow/capability/flow-variables execution patterns (user/system-flow-runner references, product capability imports, user/system-flow-execution entry-point calls, declared-user/system-flow-sequence executor loops, flow variables carry/mutation), with the concrete runner names, entry-point call and sequence field supplied by the profile. The check's findings (missing runner, boundary violation) are outputs of the check, not activation prerequisites: once the prerequisites hold, the check runs over the user/system flows runtime layer even when that layer or the journey runner does not exist yet.
Enforcement: severity 4, disposition strict (as stated in the source; no further enforcement semantics implied).

Definitions used by the check: journey runner = the runtime continuation-control layer that traverses declared journey topology between flow routers; the boundary = journey runner -> flow router runner -> user/system flow runner, each layer owning only its declared responsibility.

Existence and boundary are one deliverable, carried operatively in then: a repository that declares journey topology plan artifacts must ship a journey runner in the user/system flows runtime layer, with the same two exceptions as the rule's unless clauses. The check does not flag the flow router runner delegating its selected user/system flow to the user/system flow runner, or the user/system flow runner executing product capability steps: those are their own responsibilities.

fires: A repository with a composition root and journey topology plan artifacts, where the journey runner (or the whole user/system flows runtime layer) is missing.

A repository with a composition root and journey topology plan artifacts, whose journey runner imports a product capability module, invokes the user/system-flow-execution entry point, references the user/system flow runner, or loops over the declared user/system flow sequence as an executor.
A repository with a composition root and journey topology plan artifacts, whose journey runner constructs a flow router runner from a hardcoded literal path.
A repository with a composition root and journey topology plan artifacts, whose journey runner carries or mutates flow variables.
A repository with a composition root and journey topology plan artifacts, whose journey runner never parses a journey declaration or never references the flow router runner.
doesNotFire: A repository with no journey topology plan artifacts.
A repository still in the planning stage with no composition root.
A consumer of a different stack, even with journey topology plan artifacts.

The flow router runner delegating its selected user/system flow to the user/system flow runner, or the user/system flow runner iterating the declared user/system flow sequence to execute product capability steps (their own responsibilities).

profileRequirements.meaning: The core speaks of the composition root role; the profile supplies the stack's local name for that role.
Path pattern of one plan artifact under the plan root; instantiated here for journey topology documents, whose presence enables the journey runner obligation.
Where the runtime user/system flows layer (journey runner, flow router runner, user/system flow runner) lives, i.e. where the journey runner must be shipped and scanned.
The stack's construct and local name for the journey runner, the continuation-control layer the core requires to be shipped.

The stack's construct and local name for the flow router runner, including its routing entry methods, which the journey runner must reference for every routing decision and must never construct from a literal path.
The stack's construct and local name for the user/system flow runner (the sole wagon-step executor), including its execution method, which the journey runner must never reference or invoke.
The stack's entry point for executing a declared user/system flow, which the journey runner must never invoke.
How the declared wagon-step sequence of a user/system flow is expressed in the runtime/plan schema, which the journey runner must not loop over as an executor.

bunOnly.text: language fact, values [bun]; note: 'Bun consumer repository (Bun runtime/lockfile/config). TypeScript alone does NOT qualify; a non-Bun TypeScript consumer is out of scope.'
bunOnly.reason: The consumer-stack gate (Bun runtime, excluding non-Bun TypeScript) is a property of the ATDD-Bun realization; the neutral core applies to consumers of whatever stack instantiates it, so each realization is scoped to its own stack by construction.
Finding ids of this rule's detector are realization details; the core's verification names the findings generically (missing runner, boundary violation).

bunOnly.reason: Enumerates other runtimes and languages to bound the ATDD-Bun consumer scope; the core states the carve-out stack-neutrally ('a consumer of a different stack').

neutralityNotes: The railway vocabulary (journey runner, flow router runner, user/system flow runner, flow variables, product capability, flow router, composition root, journey topology) is treated as stack-neutral ATDD domain language, consistent with vocabulary.yaml's user-system-flow/capability/journey artifact params. Every concrete value the core needs comes from the profile: the composition-root local name (roles.composition_root.name), the journey plan-artifact path (the existing layout.plan_item key, replacing the r1 proposal that duplicated it), the user/system-flows-layer location (proposed roles.runtime_components#user_system_flows_location), and — per the r2 feedback — the runner constructs/names with their entry-method signatures plus the user/system-flow-execution entry point and the declared-sequence field (proposed roles.runtime_components#journey_runner, roles.runtime_components#flow_router_runner, roles.runtime_components#user_system_flow_runner, roles.runtime_components#user_system_flow_execution_entry, idiom.plan_syntax#declared_user_system_flow_sequence), so other stacks can map their own runner chain, execution call and sequence field instead of those values being Bun-only. What remains bunOnly is genuinely realization-specific: the consumer-stack gate (language=bun, with the non-Bun / non-Bun-TypeScript carve-outs in doesNotFire), this rule's detector finding ids, and the sibling rule id coder.bun.flow-router-runner-exists. Per-rule severity and disposition stay in core verification, not the profile. The consumer-stack gate cannot be expressed in the neutral core: each realization is scoped to its own stack's consumers by construction.
